terms.gloss: noisy, always shouting; full of noise
evidence: Quint. 6.4.15: turbidus et clāmōsus altercātor (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of people who shout, and of places full of shouting. Mostly post-Augustan (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Plaut. Trin. 5.2.52: tam tumultuōsō sonitū (Lewis & Short)
Prud. Cath. 1.13: vōx ista quā strepunt avēs
terms.comment: Latin often says “noisy” with this verb.

phrases.latin: jam trīstis nucibus puer relictīs clāmōsō revocātur ā magistrō
phrases.english: now the sad boy leaves his nuts and is called back by the shouting schoolmaster

phrases.latin: vōx ista quā strepunt avēs stantēs sub ipsō culmine
phrases.english: that chatter the birds make, perched under the ridge of the roof
Why are you so noisy, children? The baby is asleep.

sources: Lewis & Short: clamosus · Lewis & Short: tumultuosus · Lewis & Short: strepo
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. noisy.
